- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

    "design": "Recon 2026-07-25 (codex scout, verified against bd-main HEAD): issue STILL REPRODUCES.\n\nConnect path: doltserver.EnsureGlobalDatabase (bd-main/internal/doltserver/doltserver.go:1215), called by shared `bd init` at cmd/bd/init.go:1200-1215. Its whole acceptance sequence is sql.Open -\u003e PingContext -\u003e CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS `beads_global`. PingContext is strictly reachability: no server UUID, no sentinel table, no schema/version probe. Startup readiness (doltserver.go:1515) is TCP-dial-only too.\n\nWhy the existing verifier does not cover this: DoltStore project-identity verification (internal/storage/dolt/store.go:1259) is gated behind `if !cfg.CreateIfMissing`, and the global initializer passes CreateIfMissing:true (cmd/bd/init.go:2827-2837), so it is bypassed exactly on the creation path. The verifier also soft-skips on missing local metadata or empty _project_id (store.go:1305-1334).\n\nPrior art: 9d7ae74a (2026-07-19, \"Adopt server identity in bd init against an authenticating gateway\", #4823) explicitly states \"Because init opens with CreateIfMissing the storage identity verifier is skipped\" - it adopts identity for the gateway case only. 0b6249b (#4952) is shared-server PID drift, unrelated. Nothing since 2026-07-07 closes this.\n\nTWO SEPARABLE PIECES - do not conflate:\n\n(A) NARROW, mechanical, no new design: when the target database ALREADY EXISTS, run verifyProjectIdentity/verifyGlobalProjectIdentity even though CreateIfMissing=true. newServerMode already holds cfg.BeadsDir, cfg.Database and the live *sql.DB at store.go:1198-1238. This blocks adopting a foreign EXISTING beads database with a different _project_id. input.content:
# P0 queue triage + PR 5143 conflict resolution — 2026-07-29

Session scope: work `bd ready`, batching and delegating, with a freshness check
against the GitHub repo before starting anything. Plus minor housekeeping.

Two pieces of work landed: the `mybd-rr4x` merge block was a real code conflict
that needed a design call to resolve, and the P0 lane audit (`mybd-6ozys`) is
complete — the P0 tier went from **7 beads to 1**.

## 1. Freshness check changed what was worth doing

Checking upstream before starting was load-bearing this session, not ceremony:

| PR | Bead | State at session start |
|----|------|------------------------|
| 5142 | mybd-2qegi | **MERGED** (bead already closed by another actor) |
| 5146 | mybd-a4h6s | **MERGED** (bead already closed by another actor) |
| 5143 | mybd-rr4x | **OPEN, `CONFLICTING`** — the actual merge block |

Two of the three PRs the control-plane memory described as in-flight were
already done. Only 5143 needed a session.

## 2. PR 5143 — the conflict was a genuine semantic collision, not a rebase chore

`mybd-rr4x` had been relabeled `merge-blocked` by the patrol with
`transition=preflight-policy`, i.e. handed back for agent judgment. The cause:
`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`.

While 5143 sat open, upstream **#5042** landed its own change to the *same
function signature*. Both PRs added a `bool` return to `openServerConnection`:

- **#5042's `created`** — "THIS call's bare `CREATE DATABASE` won the ownership
  arbitration". Threaded to `initSchema` so only the proven creator arms
  `schema.WithFreshBootstrapHeal`.
- **5143's `dbAlreadyExisted`** — "the database was proven to exist before this
  call". Forces project-identity verification even when `CreateIfMissing` is
  true (GH#4637).

The tempting resolution is to keep one and derive the other, since across most
paths they are inverses. **They are not inverses**, and the place they diverge
is the one that matters:

> On the **Gateway** branch, existence is never probed. Both signals must be
> `false` there. `!created` would evaluate to `true` — wrongly forcing identity
> verification on a gateway open, which is the exact case 5143 documents as
> deliberately excluded (gateway identity is *reconciled* by
> `resolveInitProjectID`, not *enforced* at open).

Collapsing them would have silently broken gateway `init`, including re-init.

### Resolution

`openServerConnection` now returns a `serverConnFacts{created, alreadyExisted}`
struct rather than a bare bool, with the non-inverse relationship documented **on
the type** — specifically so a future cleanup pass does not "simplify" one field
into the other and reintroduce the gateway break.

Also folded in during the rebase: the identity gate stays **above** `initSchema`
(so a foreign database is rejected before bd writes DDL and Dolt commits into
it), and the moved `initSchema` call now carries #5042's `created` argument.

### Verification on the rebased head `b40f0a3c6`

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean.
- `go test ./internal/storage/dolt/ -run 'CrossProject|ProjectIdentity|Identity|FreshBootstrapHeal|Gateway'`
  → **18 pass, 0 fail**.

That deliberately includes **#5042's own** `TestFreshBootstrapHealNotArmedWhenDatabasePreexists`
and `TestFreshBootstrapHealSelfHealsAfterMidPassFailure` — the tests this
resolution could plausibly have broken — alongside 5143's six identity cases
(foreign-rejected, matching-succeeds, new-database, both soft-skips, and the
gateway-skip pin).

PR is now `MERGEABLE`. `make test` re-enqueued to the verify queue; merge tail
re-handed to the pr-babysit patrol. Explanatory comment posted upstream.

## 3. P0 lane audit (`mybd-6ozys`) — 7 → 1

Every one of the six P0s got a recorded disposition with a stated re-escalation
trigger. Upstream freshness was re-checked in-session for all five backing
issues: **all still OPEN, none referenced by any merged commit on
`upstream/main` (423afdcb2)** — so nothing was quietly fixed. But four of the
five have **zero upstream comments** since May/June.

| Bead | Issue | Disposition | Why |
|------|-------|-------------|-----|
| mybd-rr4x | 4637 | **KEEP P0**, claimed, active | Fix in flight (above) |
| mybd-rqqa2 | 4052 | **KEEP P0** | Only one with first-party verification vs current main (2026-07-27 @ c989b6b87) |
| mybd-sc70 | 4379 | P0 → **P1**, consolidated under `mybd-rqqa2` | Same defect, reported from the other side |
| mybd-tgqsj | 3905 | P0 → **P1**, consolidated under `mybd-agf58` | Unverified v1.0.4-era, 0 comments |
| mybd-mznh | 4381 | P0 → **P1**, consolidated under `mybd-agf58` | Unverified v1.0.x-era, 0 comments |
| mybd-1hao | 4521 | P0 → **P1**, `human` retained | Blocked on an owner design call since 2026-07-17 |

### The finding behind the downgrades

P0 had drifted to mean *"severity if the report is true"* rather than *"verified
critical"*. Two tests now applied:

1. **Is it verified against current main by us**, not merely reported?
2. **May an agent act on it today**, or is it human-gated?

`mybd-1hao` is the clearest case of the second: severe (journal corruption), but
correctly blocked since 2026-07-17 because `manifest_recovery.go` holds an
explicit stance *against* auto-repair for this case, and reversing that is not
an agent's call. A P0 no agent may act on is queue noise — it displaces
verified work and erodes what P0 means.

The first test matters because of a specific local prior: the **v1.1.2 write-path
rework invalidated many v1.0.3/1.0.4-era reports**. Sibling `mybd-5vvos` — a
consolidated *six*-failure-mode data-integrity report in the same family as
3905/4381 — was verified **FIXED on v1.1.2** on 2026-07-28, trigger mechanism
removed. So "reproduce against current main first" is the right gate for the
whole family, and `mybd-agf58`'s acceptance already requires it.

Two consolidation vehicles already existed and were reused rather than
duplicated: `mybd-agf58` (embedded-mode silent lost-write family, umbrella
gh 4135) and `mybd-rqqa2` (unreachable-server write path). `related` dep edges
were added so the links are visible to `bd`, not just prose.

**Caveat carried forward on `mybd-sc70`:** its proposed remedy — the always-on
offline write-spool carried on our fork — was reviewed as PR 4520 and **closed
upstream 2026-07-27** as REDESIGN/DECLINE (two confirmed correctness blockers
plus a storage-boundary violation). Whoever picks up `mybd-rqqa2` should not
re-propose the spool without engaging that review; the direction should be
fail-closed on the write path, not buffer-and-replay.

**Cheapest next probe**, recorded on `mybd-mznh`: its fallback triggers on
*missing config*, so the repro is "rename the config key, watch which database
the write lands in" — no concurrency harness needed. That is the fastest way to
prove or kill the whole `mybd-agf58` family.

## 4. Delegation note — a scout run that returned nothing

The P0 freshness recon was first delegated to `codex-agent scout`. It came back
**100% UNVERIFIED** on all five issues, for two compounding reasons:

1. `codex-agent scout` runs `sandbox=read-only`, so `git fetch` fails (cannot
   write `FETCH_HEAD`). The prompt had asked it to refresh `upstream/main`.
2. The GitHub API was intermittently unreachable from this machine — visible
   independently in the pr-babysit patrol log, which logged repeated
   `error connecting to api.github.com` and skipped sweeps.

Redone in-session as one Bash call with a retry loop: five `gh issue view` calls,
all five resolved on the first or second try.

The scout behaved **correctly** — it was told to retry then mark UNVERIFIED
rather than guess, and it did exactly that. The fault was in the prompt. Rules
recorded as `bd remember scout-codex-readonly-no-fetch`:

- Never put "fetch upstream" in a scout prompt. Refresh refs in the orchestrator
  *before* delegating; tell the scout to read existing refs only.
- For gh-dependent recon, either give an explicit retry-then-UNVERIFIED
  instruction, or just run the loop in-session — five `gh` calls cost far less
  than a delegation round-trip that returns nothing.

## 5. Housekeeping

- Removed two now-dead beads worktrees whose PRs merged today and whose trees
  were clean: `.worktrees/beads/doctor-fix-port` (#5142) and
  `.worktrees/beads/draincall-tx` (#5146). Branches retained.
- Stash stack empty; no local branches with a `gone` upstream; verify-log
  buildup only 656K. Nothing else needed action.

### What I noticed that isn't on any list

**The pr-babysit patrol is degrading silently under network failure.** The
patrol log shows `gh pr view failed or returned malformed data; retained
silently (3/10)` and `(4/10)` across several beads, plus
`review: gh pr list failed; sweep skipped`. That is the intended
unreadable-checks retry budget working as designed — but the budget is being
consumed by a *local network outage*, not by anything about those PRs. If the
outage persists across ~10 passes (~2h), beads will hit `merge-blocked` /
`close-blocked` for a reason that has nothing to do with their state, and a
human gets paged for a Wi-Fi problem.

Not fixed here, and not obviously worth fixing — but worth someone deciding
deliberately: a connection error is distinguishable from malformed data, and
arguably should pause the patrol rather than spend a bead's retry budget. Filed
as **`mybd-4b8ac`**.

## Handoff

- **`mybd-rqqa2` is the single actionable unclaimed P0** and is real engineering
  work, not triage. Fix direction: make the auto-start fallback fail the write
  rather than silently retarget it. Read the PR 4520 caveat above first.
- `mybd-rr4x` stays claimed and `in_progress` until the patrol merges 5143.
- `mybd-agf58` is now the single entry point for the embedded-mode silent
  lost-write family; start with the `mybd-mznh` missing-config probe.

# P0 queue triage + PR 5143 conflict resolution — 2026-07-29

Session scope: work `bd ready`, batching and delegating, with a freshness check
against the GitHub repo before starting anything. Plus minor housekeeping.

Two pieces of work landed: the `mybd-rr4x` merge block was a real code conflict
that needed a design call to resolve, and the P0 lane audit (`mybd-6ozys`) is
complete — the P0 tier went from **7 beads to 1**.

## 1. Freshness check changed what was worth doing

Checking upstream before starting was load-bearing this session, not ceremony:

| PR | Bead | State at session start |
|----|------|------------------------|
| 5142 | mybd-2qegi | **MERGED** (bead already closed by another actor) |
| 5146 | mybd-a4h6s | **MERGED** (bead already closed by another actor) |
| 5143 | mybd-rr4x | **OPEN, `CONFLICTING`** — the actual merge block |

Two of the three PRs the control-plane memory described as in-flight were
already done. Only 5143 needed a session.

## 2. PR 5143 — the conflict was a genuine semantic collision, not a rebase chore

`mybd-rr4x` had been relabeled `merge-blocked` by the patrol with
`transition=preflight-policy`, i.e. handed back for agent judgment. The cause:
`mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`.

While 5143 sat open, upstream **#5042** landed its own change to the *same
function signature*. Both PRs added a `bool` return to `openServerConnection`:

- **#5042's `created`** — "THIS call's bare `CREATE DATABASE` won the ownership
  arbitration". Threaded to `initSchema` so only the proven creator arms
  `schema.WithFreshBootstrapHeal`.
- **5143's `dbAlreadyExisted`** — "the database was proven to exist before this
  call". Forces project-identity verification even when `CreateIfMissing` is
  true (GH#4637).

The tempting resolution is to keep one and derive the other, since across most
paths they are inverses. **They are not inverses**, and the place they diverge
is the one that matters:

> On the **Gateway** branch, existence is never probed. Both signals must be
> `false` there. `!created` would evaluate to `true` — wrongly forcing identity
> verification on a gateway open, which is the exact case 5143 documents as
> deliberately excluded (gateway identity is *reconciled* by
> `resolveInitProjectID`, not *enforced* at open).

Collapsing them would have silently broken gateway `init`, including re-init.

### Resolution

`openServerConnection` now returns a `serverConnFacts{created, alreadyExisted}`
struct rather than a bare bool, with the non-inverse relationship documented **on
the type** — specifically so a future cleanup pass does not "simplify" one field
into the other and reintroduce the gateway break.

Also folded in during the rebase: the identity gate stays **above** `initSchema`
(so a foreign database is rejected before bd writes DDL and Dolt commits into
it), and the moved `initSchema` call now carries #5042's `created` argument.

### Verification on the rebased head `b40f0a3c6`

- `go build ./...` and `go vet` clean.
- `go test ./internal/storage/dolt/ -run 'CrossProject|ProjectIdentity|Identity|FreshBootstrapHeal|Gateway'`
  → **18 pass, 0 fail**.

That deliberately includes **#5042's own** `TestFreshBootstrapHealNotArmedWhenDatabasePreexists`
and `TestFreshBootstrapHealSelfHealsAfterMidPassFailure` — the tests this
resolution could plausibly have broken — alongside 5143's six identity cases
(foreign-rejected, matching-succeeds, new-database, both soft-skips, and the
gateway-skip pin).

PR is now `MERGEABLE`. `make test` re-enqueued to the verify queue; merge tail
re-handed to the pr-babysit patrol. Explanatory comment posted upstream.

## 3. P0 lane audit (`mybd-6ozys`) — 7 → 1

Every one of the six P0s got a recorded disposition with a stated re-escalation
trigger. Upstream freshness was re-checked in-session for all five backing
issues: **all still OPEN, none referenced by any merged commit on
`upstream/main` (423afdcb2)** — so nothing was quietly fixed. But four of the
five have **zero upstream comments** since May/June.

| Bead | Issue | Disposition | Why |
|------|-------|-------------|-----|
| mybd-rr4x | 4637 | **KEEP P0**, claimed, active | Fix in flight (above) |
| mybd-rqqa2 | 4052 | **KEEP P0** | Only one with first-party verification vs current main (2026-07-27 @ c989b6b87) |
| mybd-sc70 | 4379 | P0 → **P1**, consolidated under `mybd-rqqa2` | Same defect, reported from the other side |
| mybd-tgqsj | 3905 | P0 → **P1**, consolidated under `mybd-agf58` | Unverified v1.0.4-era, 0 comments |
| mybd-mznh | 4381 | P0 → **P1**, consolidated under `mybd-agf58` | Unverified v1.0.x-era, 0 comments |
| mybd-1hao | 4521 | P0 → **P1**, `human` retained | Blocked on an owner design call since 2026-07-17 |

### The finding behind the downgrades

P0 had drifted to mean *"severity if the report is true"* rather than *"verified
critical"*. Two tests now applied:

1. **Is it verified against current main by us**, not merely reported?
2. **May an agent act on it today**, or is it human-gated?

`mybd-1hao` is the clearest case of the second: severe (journal corruption), but
correctly blocked since 2026-07-17 because `manifest_recovery.go` holds an
explicit stance *against* auto-repair for this case, and reversing that is not
an agent's call. A P0 no agent may act on is queue noise — it displaces
verified work and erodes what P0 means.

The first test matters because of a specific local prior: the **v1.1.2 write-path
rework invalidated many v1.0.3/1.0.4-era reports**. Sibling `mybd-5vvos` — a
consolidated *six*-failure-mode data-integrity report in the same family as
3905/4381 — was verified **FIXED on v1.1.2** on 2026-07-28, trigger mechanism
removed. So "reproduce against current main first" is the right gate for the
whole family, and `mybd-agf58`'s acceptance already requires it.

Two consolidation vehicles already existed and were reused rather than
duplicated: `mybd-agf58` (embedded-mode silent lost-write family, umbrella
gh 4135) and `mybd-rqqa2` (unreachable-server write path). `related` dep edges
were added so the links are visible to `bd`, not just prose.

**Caveat carried forward on `mybd-sc70`:** its proposed remedy — the always-on
offline write-spool carried on our fork — was reviewed as PR 4520 and **closed
upstream 2026-07-27** as REDESIGN/DECLINE (two confirmed correctness blockers
plus a storage-boundary violation). Whoever picks up `mybd-rqqa2` should not
re-propose the spool without engaging that review; the direction should be
fail-closed on the write path, not buffer-and-replay.

**Cheapest next probe**, recorded on `mybd-mznh`: its fallback triggers on
*missing config*, so the repro is "rename the config key, watch which database
the write lands in" — no concurrency harness needed. That is the fastest way to
prove or kill the whole `mybd-agf58` family.

## 4. Delegation note — a scout run that returned nothing

The P0 freshness recon was first delegated to `codex-agent scout`. It came back
**100% UNVERIFIED** on all five issues, for two compounding reasons:

1. `codex-agent scout` runs `sandbox=read-only`, so `git fetch` fails (cannot
   write `FETCH_HEAD`). The prompt had asked it to refresh `upstream/main`.
2. The GitHub API was intermittently unreachable from this machine — visible
   independently in the pr-babysit patrol log, which logged repeated
   `error connecting to api.github.com` and skipped sweeps.

Redone in-session as one Bash call with a retry loop: five `gh issue view` calls,
all five resolved on the first or second try.

The scout behaved **correctly** — it was told to retry then mark UNVERIFIED
rather than guess, and it did exactly that. The fault was in the prompt. Rules
recorded as `bd remember scout-codex-readonly-no-fetch`:

- Never put "fetch upstream" in a scout prompt. Refresh refs in the orchestrator
  *before* delegating; tell the scout to read existing refs only.
- For gh-dependent recon, either give an explicit retry-then-UNVERIFIED
  instruction, or just run the loop in-session — five `gh` calls cost far less
  than a delegation round-trip that returns nothing.

## 5. Housekeeping

- Removed two now-dead beads worktrees whose PRs merged today and whose trees
  were clean: `.worktrees/beads/doctor-fix-port` (#5142) and
  `.worktrees/beads/draincall-tx` (#5146). Branches retained.
- Stash stack empty; no local branches with a `gone` upstream; verify-log
  buildup only 656K. Nothing else needed action.

### What I noticed that isn't on any list

**The pr-babysit patrol is degrading silently under network failure.** The
patrol log shows `gh pr view failed or returned malformed data; retained
silently (3/10)` and `(4/10)` across several beads, plus
`review: gh pr list failed; sweep skipped`. That is the intended
unreadable-checks retry budget working as designed — but the budget is being
consumed by a *local network outage*, not by anything about those PRs. If the
outage persists across ~10 passes (~2h), beads will hit `merge-blocked` /
`close-blocked` for a reason that has nothing to do with their state, and a
human gets paged for a Wi-Fi problem.

Not fixed here, and not obviously worth fixing — but worth someone deciding
deliberately: a connection error is distinguishable from malformed data, and
arguably should pause the patrol rather than spend a bead's retry budget. Filed
as **`mybd-4b8ac`**.

## Handoff

- **`mybd-rqqa2` is the single actionable unclaimed P0** and is real engineering
  work, not triage. Fix direction: make the auto-start fallback fail the write
  rather than silently retarget it. Read the PR 4520 caveat above first.
- `mybd-rr4x` stays claimed and `in_progress` until the patrol merges 5143.
- `mybd-agf58` is now the single entry point for the embedded-mode silent
  lost-write family; start with the `mybd-mznh` missing-config probe.

deliberately: a connection error is distinguishable from malformed data, and
arguably should pause the patrol rather than spend a bead's retry budget. Filed
-as **`mybd-4b8ac`**.
+as **`mybd-ihsnv`**.
## Handoff

Why the existing identity gate does not catch it: verifyProjectIdentity compares local metadata.json _project_id against the DB's _project_id. ## The defect (upstream gastownhall/beads issue 4052)

In server mode, when the Dolt server at the configured port is unreachable, bd auto-starts a NEW server on an EPHEMERAL port serving the local `.beads` dir, prints only a stderr warning, overwrites `cfg.ServerPort`, and proceeds. The user's write lands in whatever database that new server serves, with exit 0 and a success message. If the original server was serving a different directory (shared-server / multi-project host), the write silently goes somewhere else.

The relevant code is `newServerMode` in `internal/storage/dolt/store.go` — the `if dialErr != nil` block, roughly lines 1476-1500, specifically the `if port != cfg.ServerPort` branch that prints `"Warning: Dolt server endpoint changed: port %d → %d (auto-start)"` and then assigns `cfg.ServerPort = port`.

## Why it must NOT simply fail closed

Retargeting is correct and desirable in the common single-repo case where the recorded port is just a stale ephemeral leftover. Failing closed unconditionally would be a bad UX regression. The distinguisher is the PORT'S PROVENANCE:

- **Authoritative** (user asserted where the server is): env var, project `config.yaml` `dolt.port`, global config `dolt.port`. Silently using a different port is WRONG here -> fail closed.
- **bd's own bookkeeping**: the gitignored `.beads/dolt-server.port` file, which bd itself writes. Replacing it freely is fine -> keep today's retarget behavior.

## Spec

1. In `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go`, `DefaultConfig(beadsDir string) *Config` (around line 520-570) already resolves the port via four SEPARATE early-return branches: env var (~line 535), port file (~546), project config.yaml (~551), global config (~559). Add a `PortSource` field to `doltserver.Config` and set it in each branch. Use a small named string type with exported constants (e.g. `PortSourceEnv`, `PortSourcePortFile`, `PortSourceConfigYaml`, `PortSourceGlobalConfig`, `PortSourceUnset`). Set it consistently — including the "no port resolved" case.

2. In `internal/storage/dolt/store.go`, the port-resolution block around lines 1211-1241 currently discards provenance by taking only `.Port` from `DefaultConfig`. Capture the source too, in a local variable available to the auto-start branch below. Note the env-var read at ~1218-1226 happens in store.go BEFORE `DefaultConfig` is consulted — a port from that read is also authoritative, so make sure it is recorded as such.

3. In the auto-start branch, when `port != cfg.ServerPort` AND `cfg.ServerPort > 0` AND the source is authoritative, return an error INSTEAD of warning-and-retargeting. Before returning, release the auto-start ref if one was acquired (follow the existing failure path a few lines below, which calls `autoStartRelease(autoStartedDir)`) so we do not leak the refcount. The error message must name both ports, say the configured server was unreachable and that bd will not silently use a different one, and give the user actionable options (start the server manually with `bd dolt start`, or remove/change the pinned port). Match the style of the neighbouring multi-line error messages in this file.

4. When the source is the port file, or `cfg.ServerPort == 0` (never resolved), behavior is UNCHANGED from today.

## Tests (required)

Add Go tests covering, at minimum:
- authoritative source + port change -> open FAILS with the new error (this is the regression test; it must genuinely discriminate — verify it FAILS if you revert your store.go change).
- port-file source + port change -> open still SUCCEEDS (guards against the UX regression).
- `cfg.ServerPort == 0` -> unaffected.
- a `DefaultConfig` unit test asserting the correct `PortSource` for each of the four branches.

Put storage tests next to the existing server-mode tests in `internal/storage/dolt/`; follow the conventions of the tests already there (look at how they spin up or fake a server — reuse the existing helpers, do not invent a new harness).

## Build/verify commands

Build and vet with the project's required tags:
  cd /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/port-provenance
  CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...
  CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/dolt/ ./internal/doltserver/
  CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/doltserver/
  CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go -count=1 -timeout 20m ./internal/storage/dolt/ -run '<your new tests plus any server-mode/port tests>'

Do NOT run the full `make test` — that is handled separately by a verification queue.

Also grep for other callers of `doltserver.DefaultConfig` and confirm adding a field breaks nothing (it is a struct field addition, so it should be additive — but check for struct literals of `doltserver.Config` that use unkeyed fields, which WOULD break).

## Commit

One commit, conventional-commit style, subject line starting `fix(dolt):`. Explain in the body WHY provenance is the distinguisher and why unconditional fail-closed was rejected. End the message with this exact trailer line:

Retargeting is correct and desirable in the common single-repo case where the recorded port is just a stale ephemeral leftover. Failing closed unconditionally would be a bad UX regression. The distinguisher is the PORT'S PROVENANCE:

- **Authoritative** (user asserted where the server is): env var, project `config.yaml` `dolt.port`, global config `dolt.port`. Silently using a different port is WRONG here -> fail closed.
- **bd's own bookkeeping**: the gitignored `.beads/dolt-server.port` file, which bd itself writes. Replacing it freely is fine -> keep today's retarget behavior.

## Spec

1. In `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go`, `DefaultConfig(beadsDir string) *Config` (around line 520-570) already resolves the port via four SEPARATE early-return branches: env var (~line 535), port file (~546), project config.yaml (~551), global config (~559). Add a `PortSource` field to `doltserver.Config` and set it in each branch. Use a small named string type with exported constants (e.g. `PortSourceEnv`, `PortSourcePortFile`, `PortSourceConfigYaml`, `PortSourceGlobalConfig`, `PortSourceUnset`). Set it consistently — including the "no port resolved" case.

2. In `internal/storage/dolt/store.go`, the port-resolution block around lines 1211-1241 currently discards provenance by taking only `.Port` from `DefaultConfig`. Capture the source too, in a local variable available to the auto-start branch below. Note the env-var read at ~1218-1226 happens in store.go BEFORE `DefaultConfig` is consulted — a port from that read is also authoritative, so make sure it is recorded as such.

3. In the auto-start branch, when `port != cfg.ServerPort` AND `cfg.ServerPort > 0` AND the source is authoritative, return an error INSTEAD of warning-and-retargeting. Before returning, release the auto-start ref if one was acquired (follow the existing failure path a few lines below, which calls `autoStartRelease(autoStartedDir)`) so we do not leak the refcount. The error message must name both ports, say the configured server was unreachable and that bd will not silently use a different one, and give the user actionable options (start the server manually with `bd dolt start`, or remove/change the pinned port). Match the style of the neighbouring multi-line error messages in this file.

4. When the source is the port file, or `cfg.ServerPort == 0` (never resolved), behavior is UNCHANGED from today.

## Tests (required)

Add Go tests covering, at minimum:
- authoritative source + port change -> open FAILS with the new error (this is the regression test; it must genuinely discriminate — verify it FAILS if you revert your store.go change).
- port-file source + port change -> open still SUCCEEDS (guards against the UX regression).
- `cfg.ServerPort == 0` -> unaffected.
- a `DefaultConfig` unit test asserting the correct `PortSource` for each of the four branches.

Put storage tests next to the existing server-mode tests in `internal/storage/dolt/`; follow the conventions of the tests already there (look at how they spin up or fake a server — reuse the existing helpers, do not invent a new harness).

## Build/verify commands

Build and vet with the project's required tags:
  cd /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/port-provenance
  CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...
  CGO_ENABLED=1 go vet -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/dolt/ ./internal/doltserver/

Do NOT run the full `make test` — that is handled separately by a verification queue.

Also grep for other callers of `doltserver.DefaultConfig` and confirm adding a field breaks nothing (it is a struct field addition, so it should be additive — but check for struct literals of `doltserver.Config` that use unkeyed fields, which WOULD break).

One commit, conventional-commit style, subject line starting `fix(dolt):`. Explain in the body WHY provenance is the distinguisher and why unconditional fail-closed was rejected. End the message with this exact trailer line:

<result>## Summary

PR 5160 reports a real historical bug, but it was already fixed on `gastownhall/beads` main two months ago, and its numbering is the *inverse* of what shipped. Merging it would reintroduce the exact panic it claims to fix.

---

### Finding 1 — The bug is already fixed on main; the PR is 2 months stale (blocker)

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main` at `upstream/main` (423afdcb2) has no duplicate versions:

- `internal/storage/schema/migrations/0048_widen_event_value_columns.up.sql`
- `internal/storage/schema/migrations/0049_longtext_large_content_columns.up.sql`
- `internal/storage/schema/migrations/ignored/0008_widen_wisp_event_value_columns.up.sql`

Fixed by `34936e260` "fix(schema): renumber duplicate release migrations" (2026-05-28 08:15, maphew), plus comment follow-up `4a24bc3e2` (#4235).

The PR head `3073631413` has parent `ff2f6154ab1` dated **2026-05-28 08:10** — branched five minutes before the maintainer's fix, and pushed 2026-07-30. `git diff --stat upstream/main pr/5160` is 2180 files / ~94k insertions / ~246k deletions.

I verified main does not panic:
```
$ CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/schema/ -run 'TestMigration|TestNoDup|TestList|TestDuplicate' -count=1
ok  github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/schema  4.457s
```
The PR body's claim "Main currently panics before any command can run" is true of the PR's base commit, not of current main.

### Finding 2 — Merging reintroduces the collision; GitHub's `MERGEABLE` is wrong (blocker)

The PR assigns `0048`=longtext, `0049`=widen. Main assigns the opposite. `git merge-tree --write-tree upstream/main pr/5160` exits 1 with four rename/rename conflicts, and the conflicted tree contains **both** names at **both** numbers:

```
CONFLICT (rename/rename): .../0044_widen_event_value_columns.up.sql renamed to
  .../0048_widen_event_value_columns.up.sql in upstream/main and to
  .../0049_widen_event_value_columns.up.sql in pr/5160
CONFLICT (rename/rename): .../0046_longtext_large_content_columns.up.sql renamed to
  .../0049_longtext_large_content_columns.up.sql in upstream/main and to
  .../0048_longtext_large_content_columns.up.sql in pr/5160
```
`gh pr view` reports `"mergeable":"MERGEABLE"` — that is stale/unreliable here. Do not act on it. A naive "accept both" resolution lands duplicates at 48 and 49 and re-triggers `checkNoDuplicateVersions` (`bd-main/internal/storage/schema/schema.go:988`, called from `list()` at `:1017`), which `panic`s on every command. The `ignored/0005`→`0008` rename is identical on both sides and auto-merges cleanly; only the main-set pair is swapped.

### Finding 3 — Q1, already-migrated databases: no re-run/corruption from a swap, but real cross-clone skew (major, hypothetical-if-applied)

Answering the question directly with evidence: the cursor is a **high-water mark**, not a per-version applied set.

- `bd-main/internal/storage/schema/schema.go:1140` — `SELECT COALESCE(MAX(version), 0) FROM <cursorTable>`
- `bd-main/internal/storage/schema/schema.go:1146-1148` — `if current >= target { return 0, columnAdded, nil }`
- `runMigrations` applies only `minVersion < version <= upTo` (`schema.go:1170` doc comment)

So a DB already at 49 would simply skip both files. Swapping shipped numbers does **not** re-run or skip a migration on an already-migrated DB, because both bodies are already applied. Version tracking is not corrupted.

The real damage is one level up: the hash recorded per version is `sha256` of the **file contents** (`schema.go:1232-1234`), keyed by version. After a swap, a freshly-migrated clone records version 48 = longtext's hash while an existing clone has version 48 = widen's hash. `ContentHashSkew` (`bd-main/internal/storage/schema/content_skew.go:16-27`) then reports versions `[48, 49]` as skewed — the "silent schema fork" alarm from #4259 — for two clones that are in fact schema-identical. This is a permanent false positive across the entire installed base. It is the reason renumbering *shipped* migrations is only ever safe once, before release; whichever assignment shipped first (main's) has to win.

No version-keyed pre-migration repair is affected: `migration_repairs.go:22-29` dispatches only on 47 and 53.

### Finding 4 — Q2, filename-keyed dispatch would silently break (major, hypothetical-if-applied)

`bd-main/internal/storage/schema/cli_migrations.go:39`:
```go
case "0049_longtext_large_content_columns.up.sql":
    return cliMigration0049LongtextLargeContentColumns
```
This is a `switch` on filename with `default: return sqlText` (`cli_migrations.go:62`). Renaming that file to `0048_...` makes the case unreachable and silently falls through to the raw source SQL — no compile error, no test naming the string. The fresh-schema CLI bundle would then use PREPARE/EXECUTE DDL that the Dolt CLI is documented (in that file's header comment) not to apply, producing a fresh-vs-runtime schema divergence. The PR does not touch this file.

Other stale references the PR would leave behind: `bd-main/internal/storage/embeddeddolt/history_test.go:11-14`, `bd-main/internal/storage/dolt/versioned_test.go:11-14` (`migration0049DDL`, explicitly cross-referencing `cliMigration0049LongtextLargeContentColumns`), and `bd-main/internal/storage/embeddeddolt/migrate_frozen_guard_convergence_test.go:49,94` (comments asserting "0048 has already widened"). These read as prose/constants, not enforced links, so they would drift silently rather than fail.

### Finding 5 — Q3, test coverage (minor)

- A test that would fail without *a* fix: yes, structurally. `checkNoDuplicateVersions` is invoked from `list()` (`schema.go:1017`), so any test that enumerates the embedded set panics. The dedicated unit test at `bd-main/internal/storage/schema/schema_test.go:190-220` only exercises synthetic `migrationFile` slices, so it does **not** guard the real embedded directory — the real gate is the incidental panic.
- A test covering the already-migrated upgrade path across a renumbering: **none exists**, in the PR or on main. That gap is what makes Finding 3 unenforced. If a renumbering is ever needed again, a test asserting content-hash stability for shipped versions would be the thing to add. Not this PR's job to fix.
- The PR adds no tests, which is correct for a pure rename, but it also means nothing would have caught the inverted assignment.

### Finding 6 — PR body's verification claims don't hold against main (nit)

The body reports `go test ./internal/storage/schema/...` passing and "a per-directory duplicate-version scan is empty after the renames." Both are true against the stale base and both are also true of unmodified current main. The evidence presented cannot distinguish the PR from a no-op.

Not `REQUEST-CHANGES` — there is no change the contributor can make that produces value here; the defect is genuinely gone. The correctness call is unambiguous: **do not merge under any resolution**, per Findings 1 and 2. The remaining question is disposition, which is a `PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.md` call — this looks like a decline-as-already-fixed (the `close-when-quiet` lane), with the contributor pointed at `34936e260`/#4235 and credited for an independently-correct diagnosis of a real bug that existed at their base commit.

<result>## Context checked

- PR 5159 metadata + full diff fetched via `gh` (no checkout); source read at `upstream/main` (423afdcb2) via `git show`.
- Existing review: `coffeegoddd` (MEMBER) **APPROVED** with comments on the escape hatch and the unrelated go.mod churn.
- CI: one FAILURE — `Test (Proxied Dolt Cmd 14/15)` → `TestProxiedServerComment/multiple_comments_ordered`: `comment_proxied_integration_test.go:122: unexpected ordering: "three", "two", "one"`. Unrelated to this change (comment timestamp-tie ordering); looks like a flake, but it should be rerun before merge, not waved through.

## What the change gets right

I checked the three gates you named against the actual call graph:

- **Migrate gate.** `schema.MigrateUpWithLock` is reachable on the proxied path from exactly one place, `internal/storage/uow/dolt_sql_provider.go:126`. The new team-server branch short-circuits *before* it and before any `CREATE DATABASE`, and returns `backoff.Permanent` for non-serialization errors, so it does not spin. This is a strict tightening, not a bypass. The integration test asserts `schema_migrations` is byte-identical after a team-server open.
- **Forward-drift guard.** `checkTeamServerSchema` delegates `current > latest` to `schema.CheckForwardDrift` (`internal/storage/uow/team_server_schema.go:29`), the same function `dolt/store.go:1598` uses. Not bypassed.
- **Remote-migrate gate.** Never ran on the proxied path in the first place (`CheckRemoteMigrateGate*` callers are only `dolt/store.go:2212` and `embeddeddolt/store.go:345`). Team-server mode removes migration entirely from that path, so it cannot regress it.
- **Fails closed on a bad target.** `openDB` pings before `initSchema`, so an unreachable server errors. Missing database → `UseDatabase` fails → "bts init". Existing-but-empty database → `CurrentVersion` returns 0 via `IsTableNotExist` → "bts init". Both are covered by the integration test. I could not construct a silent-success path.
- Reuse of `resolveInitIssuePrefix`/`resolveInitProjectID` with `gateway=true` is the right call — those gateway branches already hard-error on an absent server value and distinguish read errors from unprovisioned, which is why the "transient, not unprovisioned" tests pass.

Line numbers below are post-patch and approximate where the diff hunk doesn't pin them exactly.

## Findings

### 1. `major` — init still writes clone-local tracking state and creates a Dolt remote **in the bts-owned shared database**

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/cmd/bd/init_proxied_server.go` ~182-201 (unchanged `bootstrapParams`) → `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/internal/storage/domain/bootstrap.go:62-100`.

`SkipIdentity` suppresses only `issue_prefix` and `_project_id`. Still written to the shared `metadata` table on every teammate's init: `repo_id`, `clone_id`, `last_import_time` — and if a git origin resolves, `BootstrapProject` calls `remoteUseCase.CreateRemote(ctx, "origin", remoteURL)`, adding a Dolt remote pointing at *that teammate's* git origin to the operator's database.

The PR body's stated goal is "a second teammate's init can't clobber the project identity", but the analogous already-solved case is right there in the tree, `cmd/bd/init.go:1313-1318`:

```
// Tracking metadata (bd_version, repo_id, clone_id) is clone-local state.
// In gateway mode it must not be written into the shared, server-owned
// database: repo_id/clone_id are per-clone fingerprints and a last-init-wins
// overwrite feeds false cross-project mismatch diagnostics...
```

`doctor` and cross-project verification read `repo_id`/`clone_id` back, so this reproduces exactly the false-mismatch diagnostics that comment describes, plus an unwanted remote on shared server state.

Fix: extend `SkipIdentity` into the same predicate the gateway path uses — i.e. in team-server mode also skip `RepoID`/`CloneID`/`LastImportTime` and the remote creation, mirroring `shouldWriteInitStateToDB(cmd/bd/init.go:1191-ish)`. Cheapest shape: add `SkipInitState bool` next to `SkipIdentity`, or rename the single flag to reflect "server owns this database".

### 2. `major` (pre-existing gap, materially widened here) — no runtime project-identity verification on the proxied path

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/cmd/bd/main.go:1348-1358` short-circuits proxied mode (`return nil`) **before** the `validateWorkspaceIdentity` call at `cmd/bd/main.go:1466-1470`, and proxied mode never constructs a `DoltStore`, so `verifyProjectIdentity` / `verifyGlobalProjectIdentity` (`internal/storage/dolt/store.go:1611-1621`, `1687`, `1724`) are unreachable. I verified this is true on `upstream/main` today, so **this PR does not remove a gate**.

But it changes the exposure. Until now, proxied-server meant a per-workspace database bd itself created; the "server is serving a DIFFERENT project's database" scenario the gate was written for barely applied. `--team-server` deliberately points bd at a long-lived, shared, operator-managed database, selectable per-invocation by `--database`. Init *adopts* the identity (it cannot detect a wrong target — there is no way to assert an expected one), and nothing re-checks afterward. Gateway mode, the closest analogue, gets `verifyProjectIdentity` on every non-`CreateIfMissing` open because it goes through `DoltStore`.

Suggested fix: after `checkTeamServerSchema` passes, compare `configfile.Load(beadsDir).ProjectID` against the DB's `_project_id` and refuse on mismatch. The reader is already written — `adoptTeamServerIdentity`'s `teamServerIdentityReader` — so this is a small addition, not new machinery. I'd accept "file a follow-up bead and merge" here; I would not accept "no runtime identity check, ever, on a shared team database".

### 3. `should-fix` — `BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW` downgrades a *behind*-schema refusal on a fully **writable** connection

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/internal/storage/uow/team_server_schema.go:32-38`.

The precedent this mirrors, `schema.CheckBehindDrift` (`internal/storage/schema/schema.go:186-209`), is explicitly documented "Used by read-only opens, which skip MigrateUp by design"; its escape hatch downgrades a *read* risk. Here the same env var lets a newer `bd` proceed to **write** against an older bts schema — INSERTs/UPDATEs naming columns the database does not have. That's a different risk class than "some queries may fail".

Also note `--ignore-schema-skew` sets `BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW` (`cmd/bd/main.go:690`, `922`), so a user who set the flag for an unrelated read now silently gets write permission against a stale schema.

Suggested fix: in team-server mode, honor the escape hatch only for read-only commands, or not at all for the behind case (forward-drift/ahead is the case where the hatch genuinely helps a stale binary read). This appears to overlap coffeegoddd's review comment "One comment, re the escape hatch" — worth reading that thread before duplicating it.

### 4. `minor` — team-server-ness is keyed to the workspace, not to the database

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/cmd/bd/uow_factory.go:22-30`: `teamServer` comes from `persisted.IsTeamServerManaged()`, while `database` can be replaced wholesale by `databaseOverride` (`--database` / `--db`, `cmd/bd/main.go:1360-1375`).

Both directions cross the boundary: `bd --database other_db` in a team-server workspace applies bts semantics to an unrelated DB (fail-closed — it refuses to create it — so this direction is benign), and a *non*-team-server proxied workspace pointed at the bts database with `--database` will happily run `MigrateUpWithLock` against the operator's schema. The second is the dangerous one and is not new, but `--team-server` is what makes "there is an operator-owned DB on this server" true.

Suggested fix: refuse `--database`/`--db` overrides that differ from the persisted `dolt_database` when `IsTeamServerManaged()`, since init already requires the name be pinned. The reverse direction is out of scope for this PR but worth a bead.

### 5. `minor` — `IsTeamServerManaged()` fails *open* outside proxied mode

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/internal/configfile/configfile.go:345-350`. `dolt_team_server: true` combined with any other `dolt_mode` silently evaluates to `false`, and "false" here means "resume migrating the operator's database". Silently-inert is the wrong default for a safety bit. The init-time guard (`cmd/bd/init.go:332-334`) means you can only reach this by hand-editing metadata.json or by a later re-init that rewrites `dolt_mode` — low likelihood, but the failure is a schema write to a shared DB.

Suggested fix: make `dolt_team_server: true` with a non-proxied `dolt_mode` a hard config error at load rather than an inert field. The PR even has a test asserting the silent-false behavior (`cmd/bd/init_proxied_server_test.go`, `TestIsTeamServerManaged_RequiresProxiedServerMode`), so this is a deliberate choice worth challenging rather than an oversight.

### 6. `minor` — the identity adoption is non-atomic, and the riskiest new block is untested

`/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main/cmd/bd/init_proxied_server.go` ~214-227 (the `configfile.Load` → set `ProjectID` → `Save` block).

metadata.json is written with a locally-minted project id *before* any connection exists; the adopted id is patched in afterward. If the reload or `Save` fails, init aborts having already mutated the shared DB (finding 1) and leaving metadata.json holding a project id that does not match the database. Because nothing verifies identity at runtime (finding 2), that state is silent rather than loud.

This block has no test — every other piece of the change is covered. Continue work in /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/port-provenance (branch fix/port-provenance-fail-closed, your commit ccba3b6f9). Same rules as before: work ONLY in that worktree, no `bd` commands, no GitHub, no push, commit locally.

Your first pass was correct for the spec you were given, and the negative control was exactly right. But review found the spec incomplete: **as written, the fix misses the defect's primary scenario — shared-server mode**, which is literally the title of the upstream issue ("Shared-server mode: write commands report success when Dolt is unreachable").

## The gap

`doltserver.DefaultConfig` (now ~line 658) begins:

```go
if IsSharedServerMode() {
    if sharedDir, err := SharedServerDir(); err == nil {
        beadsDir = sharedDir      // <-- port resolves from the SHARED dir
    }
}
```

So in shared-server mode the port comes from the **shared server directory's port file** → `PortSourcePortFile` → your `IsAuthoritative()` returns false → auto-start silently retargets. But the auto-start in `newServerMode` calls `EnsureRunningDetailed(resolvedBeadsDir)` where `resolvedBeadsDir` is the **repo's** `.beads`, not the shared dir.

Net effect today and after your patch: the shared server goes down, bd spins up a repo-local server serving a *different database*, and the write silently lands there with exit 0. That is precisely GH#4052.

There is a second uncovered branch just below, `if cfg.Port == 0 && IsSharedServerMode()`, which falls back to the fixed shared server port — that would be `PortSourceUnset`, also non-authoritative, also retargets.

## What to add

The insight: provenance is not the only axis. What also matters is **whether the resolved port belongs to a different server directory than the one auto-start would spin up**. When it does, retargeting is never a benign port refresh — it is a silent change of database.

1. Have `DefaultConfig` record that the port was resolved in shared-server mode — e.g. a `PortSharedServer bool` on `doltserver.Config` (set true whenever the `IsSharedServerMode()` swap took effect, including the `cfg.Port == 0` shared fallback branch). Prefer a separate field over a new `PortSource` constant, because it is orthogonal: a shared-mode port can come from any source.

2. Thread it into `dolt.Config` alongside `ServerPortSource` (mirror what you already did).

3. In `newServerMode`'s auto-start branch, fail closed when the port changed and **either** the source is authoritative **or** the port was shared-server-resolved. Keep the existing ref-release behavior.

4. Give the shared-server case its own error text — the operator action is different (the shared server is down and should be restarted; the fix is not "unpin a stale port"). It should say the shared Dolt server was unreachable, that auto-starting a repo-local server would write to a *different database* than the shared one, and point at `bd dolt start` / restarting the shared server. Follow the multi-line style of the neighbouring errors.

## Tests to add

- shared-server-resolved port + port change → open FAILS with the shared-server error, **including the case where the source is `PortSourcePortFile`** (this is the regression test that would have caught the gap — make sure it fails if you revert the shared-server half of the condition).
- shared-server mode with `cfg.Port == 0` falling back to the fixed shared port, then a port change → also fails closed.
- a `DefaultConfig` unit test asserting `PortSharedServer` is true in shared mode and false otherwise.
- your existing tests must still pass unchanged.

Use the same `ensureRunningDetailed` package-var stubbing pattern you introduced. For shared mode you will likely need to set `BEADS_DOLT_SHARED_SERVER=1` and point `SharedServerDir()` somewhere temporary — check how existing tests handle shared-server mode and follow that; if there is no precedent, `t.Setenv` plus whatever env var `SharedServerDir()` honors.

## Also

Re-run the same negative control discipline: verify each new regression test genuinely fails without its half of the fix, and report the result.

    property of the id itself. Every events/comments/compaction_snapshots
    insert now derives its primary key from the row's content via the shipped
    rowid derivation (frozen digest column lists, app-stamped DATETIME(0)
    created_at text bound verbatim so the stored cell is byte-for-byte what
    was digested). Events keep local multiplicity through ordinals; comments
    collapse onto an identical existing row, matching the import path's
    historical existence check. Wisp-plane and promotion-carried ids stay
    minted-once (clone-local, random-but-consistent).

    * feat(schema): catch-up aux-row rekey pass for interim UUIDv7 rows (bd-ri8bd)
    
    Rows minted between the initial bd-6dnrw.2 backfill and the switch to
    insert-time derivation carry random UUIDv7 keys. Generalize the rekey
    machinery over (marker, shipped-version, sentinel) and run it once more —
    ignored marker 0018, anchored on main 0061 so a fresh clone of a lineage
    that has converged skips the rewrite while a clone of a 0060-era lineage
    does not. Clone-local and deliberately not migrator-exclusive: the
    derivation is deterministic, so every clone converges independently (V2
    designated-migrator compatible).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    * fix(storage): keep wisp_events DEFAULT '' semantics in InsertDerivedEvent (bd-ri8bd)
    
    The pre-derivation mint sites omitted unset old_value/new_value/comment
    columns, so wisp_events rows stored the columns' DEFAULT '' while durable
    events rows stored NULL. InsertDerivedEvent binds all columns explicitly,
    which wrote NULL into wisp rows — flagged by the conformance oracle
    (Audit/labels-comments-events/EventValueNullability) and divergent from the
    digests legacy wisp rows re-derive to. Coerce unset values to '' for the
    wisp plane before digesting.

Digests are a pure function of content, so for fixed comment texts the tiebreak order is FIXED. The three texts in the test ('one','two','three') always sort to 'three','two','one' by digest. Therefore:

So what looks like flakiness is really 'did the three CLI invocations happen to cross a 1-second boundary'. On a fast runner they usually do not; on a slow/loaded one they may. content.text:
Progress report while the last two jobs finish.

**PR 5159 (`--team-server`) — reviewed and posted**

Verified all three safety gates myself before commenting: the migrate gate, forward-drift guard, and remote-migrate gate are all *tightened*, not bypassed. Approved with comments, one pre-merge ask I confirmed in the diff: `SkipIdentity` gates only `issue_prefix`/`_project_id`, so every teammate's init still writes `repo_id`/`clone_id`/`last_import_time` — and a Dolt remote pointing at *their* git origin — into the operator's shared database. The gateway path already solves exactly this 800 lines away via `shouldWriteInitStateToDB`. Structural gap filed as `mybd-xjbub`.

**The builder's first pass was incomplete — caught in review**

The port-provenance fix passed build, vet, tests, and a genuine negative control. But it missed the defect's *primary* scenario, the one in the issue's title: in shared-server mode `DefaultConfig` resolves the port from the **shared** directory's port file, which the patch classified as non-authoritative — while auto-start spins up a server from the **repo's** `.beads`. So the headline case (shared server down → write silently lands in a different database) was still broken. My spec was the incomplete part, not the builder's work. Sent back with the second axis: whether the port belongs to a *different server directory* than the one auto-start would create.

**A real regression found in today's main — `mybd-1t4fq`**

Chasing a CI failure on 5143 led somewhere more interesting. The same shard failed on 5143 *and* 5159 — so neither change caused it. It traces to #5150 (merged today, tip of main), which made comment ids **content-derived**. Comments are listed `ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC`, and `created_at` is `DATETIME(0)` — one-second precision. So comments posted in the same second now tie on the sort key and fall back to *hash order*.

It isn't flaky, it's deterministic: for fixed text the digest order is fixed, so the test fails identically whenever the three writes don't straddle a second boundary. Your two passes are correct and the negative controls were right. Review found one more hole — a sequencing bug that makes the non-shared-mode half of the fix **self-defeating after a single invocation**.

## The hole

`doltserver.Start()` writes the port file with the actual listening port — `writePortFile(beadsDir, actualPort)` at `internal/doltserver/doltserver.go:1291` on the normal start path, and also at `:1176` on the adopt-existing-server path. That happens **inside** `EnsureRunningDetailed`, i.e. BEFORE `newServerMode` reaches your fail-closed check.

The port file is the *second-highest* precedence source, above `config.yaml` and `metadata.json`. So in NON-shared mode with an authoritative `config.yaml` `dolt.port`:

1. `bd close X` → configured port unreachable → auto-start spawns a server on ephemeral port Q → **`Start()` writes `.beads/dolt-server.port` = Q** → your check fires → error. Good so far.
2. The user retries `bd close X`. Now `DefaultConfig` resolves the port from the port file → **Q**, source `PortSourcePortFile` (non-authoritative), `PortSharedServer` false. The server on Q is running, so the dial succeeds, no auto-start branch is entered at all, and bd silently writes to the repo-local database.

So the guard fires exactly once and then permanently disarms itself. That is arguably worse than not guarding: the user sees an error, retries, it "works", and they conclude the first error was transient.

Shared-server mode is NOT affected — `DefaultConfig` swaps `beadsDir` to the shared dir, so the repo-local port file `Start()` just wrote is never consulted. Your shared-mode tests stay valid.

## What to add

On every fail-closed return in the auto-start branch (both the shared-server branch and the authoritative-source branch), leave no state behind that would let the next invocation silently succeed:

1. **Snapshot the port file before calling `EnsureRunningDetailed`** — capture its exact prior bytes, or the fact that it did not exist. Use the same path resolution the rest of the code uses (`PortFileName` / whatever helper exists — do not hand-roll the path).
2. **On the fail-closed paths, restore that snapshot**: rewrite the prior bytes, or delete the file if it did not exist before. Restore before returning the error. Preserve the file mode used elsewhere (`writePortFile` uses 0600-ish — match it).
3. **If we started the server ourselves, stop it.** `EnsureRunningDetailed` already returns `startedByUs`; it is currently only consulted for the test-only `trackAutoStartedServer` path. On the fail-closed paths, when `startedByUs` is true, stop the server we just spawned — we have decided not to use it, and leaving a stray dolt process running is a side effect the user did not ask for. Use whatever existing stop helper `doltserver` exposes (look for how `autoStartRelease` stops a server and reuse that mechanism rather than inventing one). If `startedByUs` is false we adopted a pre-existing server — do NOT stop it, just restore the port file.
4. Keep the existing `autoStartRelease` / `breaker.RecordFailure()` calls; order them sensibly (stop/restore before returning).

Best-effort semantics: if the restore or stop fails, do not mask the original fail-closed error — that error is the important one. Surface the cleanup failure as a warning on stderr at most.

Then assert that a SECOND `newServerMode` call with the same config still fails closed rather than succeeding — that is the actual user-visible bug, so test it directly.
- Same port-file-restoration assertion for the shared-server fail-closed path.
- A test that `startedByUs == true` results in the spawned server being stopped, and `startedByUs == false` leaves it alone. Extend your `ensureRunningDetailed` package-var stub to report both, and stub the stop path too if needed.
- Existing tests must still pass.

input.command:
cat > /tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/370f0275-8edd-43b8-a7c8-175b0c2f86b5/scratchpad/5150-comment.md <<'EOF'
Heads-up on a likely regression from this change — flagging rather than asserting, since I have not reproduced it locally (details on why below).

**Symptom:** `Test (Proxied Dolt Cmd 14/15)` is failing on at least two independent PRs — #5143 and #5159 — both on `cmd/bd/comment_proxied_integration_test.go:108`, `TestProxiedServerComment/multiple_comments_ordered`:

```
comment_proxied_integration_test.go:122: unexpected ordering: "three", "two", "one"
```

Neither PR touches comments, and `main`'s Nightly Full Tests was green at 03:06, so it reads as probabilistic rather than a hard break.

**Proposed mechanism:**

- Comments are listed with `ORDER BY created_at ASC, id ASC` — `internal/storage/issueops/comments.go:29` and `:88`, and `internal/storage/domain/db/comment.go:87`.
- After this PR, a comment's `id` is content-derived, and per `derivedid.go:25-27` `created_at` participates only as its **`DATETIME(0)`** text rendering — one-second granularity.
- So comments written inside the same second tie on the primary sort key, and the `id ASC` tiebreaker is now a content digest rather than anything carrying insertion order.

Since `InsertDerivedComment`'s inputs include `issueID` (`comments.go:253`), which is fresh per run, the resulting permutation varies run to run — so under a same-second tie roughly five of six runs come out wrong. `multiple_comments_ordered` writes three comments back to back, so on a fast runner it hits the tie nearly every time.

**Why I could not reproduce locally, and why that is consistent rather than contradictory:** four consecutive runs with `BEADS_TEST_PROXIED_SERVER=1` all passed here (214s for four). This box is slow enough that each `bd comment` CLI invocation lands in a *different* second, so `created_at` breaks the tie before `id` is ever consulted. It is fast runners that collide. Worth noting for anyone triaging: repeating the integration test on a slow machine will pass indefinitely and prove nothing, and a green CI re-run is luck rather than evidence the bug is gone.

A deterministic check that removes the timing variable: insert two comments with an identical explicit `created_at` second and assert their order — that exercises the actual invariant.

**If this is right, it is user-visible, not just a test issue:** any two comments posted within the same second display in digest order rather than the order they were written — easy to hit with scripted or agent-driven use.

I have deliberately not proposed a patch, because the fix interacts with this PR's convergence property and that is your design. The obvious lever — widening `created_at` precision — looks wrong here, since the commit message says the `DATETIME(0)` text is bound verbatim so the stored cell is byte-for-byte what was digested, meaning a precision change reshapes every derived id. Giving comments an explicit ordinal/sequence to order by seems closer to the intent, and this PR already says events "keep local multiplicity through ordinals" — so comments may simply have been missed. But that interacts with comments deliberately collapsing onto an identical existing row, so it is your call.

Happy to take the fix if you tell me which direction you want.

Item (3) is the cheap one that catches it.

Related: the same bead's first pass missed the shared-server case entirely because the spec framed the discriminator as one axis (port provenance) when there were two (provenance AND whether the port belongs to a different server directory than the one auto-start creates). Two agents still running. Brief status while I wait:

**Since the last update:**

- **PR 5143** now has no failing checks (the flaky shard cleared); the patrol owns the merge.
- **Comment-ordering regression reported upstream** on #5150, framed as "flagging, not asserting" — I disclosed that I *couldn't* reproduce it locally and explained why that's consistent rather than contradictory (this box is slow enough that each `bd comment` lands in a different second, so `created_at` breaks the tie before the hash does). I deliberately didn't propose a patch: the obvious lever, widening `created_at` precision, would reshape every derived id, and the design is the author's.

**I had to correct myself on that one.** I'd recorded that the wrong ordering was deterministic for fixed comment text. It isn't — `InsertDerivedComment`'s digest includes `issueID`, which is fresh per run, so the permutation varies run to run. That makes it *worse* than I first wrote: under a same-second tie, roughly five of six runs come out wrong. Corrected in the bead before reporting upstream.

**The port-provenance fix has now failed review twice**, both times on my spec rather than the builder's execution:

1. First pass missed shared-server mode — the defect's headline case — because I framed the discriminator as one axis when there were two.
2. Second pass was **self-defeating**: `Start()` writes the port file *before* the guard runs, and the port file outranks `config.yaml`, so the guard fired once and then permanently disarmed. A user would see an error, retry, and have it "work" — worse than no guard.

Third pass is in flight. The reusable lesson is recorded: any fail-closed guard needs its regression test to call the guarded path **twice**, or a self-disarming guard looks green.

Also worth knowing: `config.yaml` and `metadata.json` are **git-tracked by default** (confirmed in the project's own `.gitignore` template), so treating a pinned port as authoritative means a fresh clone that inherited one gets a hard error where today it silently auto-starts. That's a real behavior change I'll disclose in the PR rather than let it surface as a support report.
